open_points.subject: Object kind
open_points.text: `other` keeps the kind optional in meaning as in form: an object no member describes is never refused.
open_points.question: When a create or correction supplies a kind outside the closed vocabulary, must Registry refuse it, store `other`, or treat the kind as absent?
options: Refuse every supplied value outside the closed vocabulary; the owner must explicitly choose `other` or omit the kind
Normalize every unsupported supplied value to `other`
Treat every unsupported supplied value as an absent kind
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unsupported supplied values and require the owner to choose `other` or omit the kind.

witness.initial: An active project has an object whose kind is absent.
events: The owner corrects the object and supplies `warehouse` as its kind.
outcomes: Registry refuses the correction because `warehouse` is outside the closed vocabulary.
Registry accepts the correction and records `other` because no named member describes the object.
witness.observer: The owner and every reader of the corrected project

open_points.subject: Object kind model
open_points.text:
These are closed sets the specification declares; in State 6 they become
`kind: enum` or `kind: vocabulary` models without identity (SPEC_STANDARD §5).
open_points.question: Must Object kind become a `kind: enum` named type used by runtime fields, or a read-only `kind: vocabulary` spec-data model?

open_points.subject: Customer language model
open_points.text:
These are closed sets the specification declares; in State 6 they become
`kind: enum` or `kind: vocabulary` models without identity (SPEC_STANDARD §5).
open_points.question: Must Customer language become a `kind: enum` named type used by runtime fields, or a read-only `kind: vocabulary` spec-data model?

open_points.subject: M12 StoreHistory identity
open_points.text:
Durable, exactly one per store, made with the store and changed only inside
the transaction of an audit append or of the import.
open_points.question: Who creates the StoreHistory entity for a new store and for a restored store, what fact distinguishes the new history from the history captured by the backup, and from what is that identity minted?
options: Registry store initialization mints a new history identity for both a new store and every restore
A restored backup preserves the prior StoreHistory entity and its identity
The recovery boundary mints a new history identity on restore, while Registry mints one for a new store
open_points.default_guess: Registry store initialization creates a new StoreHistory entity for each new or restored store incarnation, with an opaque identity distinct from any identity captured by the backup.

open_points.subject: M12 StoreHistory lifecycle and inherited MigrationClosure
open_points.text: begun (store made new, or restored) -> number moves -> closure recorded (once)
open_points.question: Can a restored StoreHistory begin with MigrationClosure already present from a post-import backup, or must every restored history begin without it and record a closure only after it begins?
options: A restored history inherits the backup's closure and may begin with it present
Every restored history begins without a closure
A restore with a closure continues the old history, while only a restore without one begins a new history
open_points.default_guess: A restore always begins a new history from all facts in the backup, so a post-import backup creates a new history with the closure already present.

witness.initial: Production completed its one import, recorded MigrationClosure, and then made a backup.
events: The owner restores the post-import backup.
The owner attempts the import again.
outcomes: The restored history begins with the backup's MigrationClosure, so Registry refuses the import.
The restored history follows the stated lifecycle from `begun` without a closure, so Registry accepts the import and records a new closure.
